voyage.content: An annual three-day music festival. It is described officially as a festival of Advanced Music and Multimedia Art. Music is by far the main aspect of the festival. The festival runs for three days and nights, usually starting on a Thursday in the third week of June. There is a day location and a night location.

voyage.name: Monegros Desert Festival
voyage.content: The most famous and biggest one day/night electronic music festivals in Spain is in the desert of Fraga, 200 km from Barcelona. More than 40,000 people gather every July to celebrate electronic music with the best DJs representing styles from house, electro, minimal, techno, to drum&bass, dubstep, and hiphop. 20 hours non-stop, it is a unique desert experience.

voyage.name: Festes de la Mercè
voyage.content: Barcelona's main annual festival around 24 September, encompassing many events such as human towers (castellers), free live music events on the streets, firework displays, and processions of wooden giants. It is a holiday and the city offers a lot of activities to have fun. Enjoy a fountains and fireworks show at the base of the Montjuïc hill.

voyage.name: Festes de Gràcia
voyage.content: The Festes de Gracia is a Catalonian celebration, held around 15 August each year to commemorate the Assumption. During the week of festivities that mark one of Barcelona's most important fiestas, the city of Gracia explodes with fun, excitement, colour, and fireworks. Many streets are decorated by neighbours, and there is live music, food in the streets, and the parties continue all night.

voyage.name: Festes de Sants
voyage.content: Similar to Gracia's event, but smaller and later on in August. If you can't go to Gracia's event, try to go to this festival.

voyage.name: Sant Jordi
voyage.content: 23 April. Considered to be like Valentine's Day. People give roses and books around the streets. Traditionally, men give women roses and women give men books. It is one of the most popular and interesting celebrations in Catalonia.

voyage.name: Corpus
voyage.content: Late in May (Corpus Christi day). An egg shell is placed over the jet of water coming out of various fountains such that the egg "magically dances" over the water. These fountains typically are beautifully decorated with flowers and are mostly at churches, most of which are located in the city centre: Cathedral's cloister, Santa Anna, Casa de l'Ardiaca, Museu Frederic Marés, and a dozen other fountains.

voyage.name: Fira de Santa Llúcia
voyage.content: From 2/3 December to 23 December, to commemorate St. Llúcia (13 December). During this time, in front of the Cathedral, Christmas objects are sold. Some places sell Christmas trees, but most of them sell elements for making the pessebres (Nativity scenes). These include small sculptures, wooden pieces, and moss used to simulate grass. 13 December is the feast day of Santa Llucia, patron saint of fashion designers and

voyage.name: Barcelona Jazz Festival
voyage.price: Tickets prices differ for each event
voyage.content: A brighter way to celebrate the colder Autumn days, the annual Jazz festival has been running for nearly 50 years now and runs roughly from the last week in October and all the way through November

voyage.name: Revetlla de Sant Joan
voyage.content: This is the midsummer solstice celebration. It is celebrated on 23 June every year and is signified by the fireworks (there are frequent and loud amateur fireworks all night long, which may make it hard to sleep) that are permanently on display during this time.

voyage.name: Fira de Barcelona
voyage.content: There are trade events all year round in Barcelona.

voyage.name: El Corte Inglés
voyage.content: Spanning several floors and several buildings, and in several locations around town, many in Eixample and Inland Suburbs and a couple also in Ciutat Vella. You can find anything and everything in this department store, from food to pneumatics. Tax return checks are made on a separate floor of the store. See review for the whole chain in the Spain article.

voyage.name: La Boqueria
voyage.content: In Ciutat Vella. Large public market with a diverse range of goods and produce. Enjoy freshly squeezed organic fruit juices for €1.5 per cup. If you go near closing time (20:00) sellers will make you a special price (2 or 3 for €2). Closed Sundays.

voyage.name: Barcelona Eat Local Food Tours
voyage.content: A family-owned business that showcases the best of Catalan gastronomy in off-the-beaten districts of Barcelona.

voyage.name: Comer y no Bombas
voyage.content: Shares free vegan food.

voyage.name: El Glop
voyage.content: Three locations, in Eixample and Gràcia. Excellent mid-range Catalan meals. Allow about €20 per person, although you could get out of there for half of that if you let the price dictate your choice of dishes.

voyage.name: Balordi
voyage.content: Located near Plaça d’Espanya. Casual Italian street-food spot specialising in panini and handmade meatballs. Expect bold flavours and quick counter service, with a few sidewalk benches for eating in. Allow about €10–15 per person depending on your choice.

voyage.name: Palau de la Música Catalana
voyage.price: Self-guided tours €18 are the cheapest option or you could go to a concert.
voyage.content: Modernist design by Lluís Domènech i Montaner is a UNESCO World Heritage site, a masterpiece of Catalan's modernist architecture. This auditorium designed by Ramon Muntaner is the most important Modernist example in Ciutat Vella. It was the headquarters of the Orfeó Català, the oldest Catalan choir. The most beautiful part is the stalls with its fine detailing, although all the building is impressive. T

voyage.name: Basilica of Santa Maria del Mar
voyage.content: One of the most representative examples of Catalan Gothic architecture, it features a sombre but beautiful interior. The upsweeping verticality and lightness of the interior are especially surprising considering the blocky exterior surfaces. Built between 1329 and 1383, it was once was home to a Christian cult in the late 3rd century. The church is dedicated to Saint Mary of the Sea, since the quarter was dedicated t

voyage.name: Carrer Montcada
voyage.content: This street has the biggest collection of Gothic houses in Barcelona. In amongst these houses is the Picasso Museum, which is definitely worth a visit. There are also smaller museums along the street, and many tapas restaurants though they may be more expensive on this street.

voyage.name: Passeig del Born
voyage.content: This avenue goes from the Santa Maria del Mar church to the Born market and is where the legendary jousting matches of the Middle Ages took place, as well as numerous fairs and marches. This is also where men were knighted. It is a really old street, very wide for the time. Don Quijote de la Mancha, the famous Cervantes character, had a contest in this place.

voyage.name: Mercat del Born
voyage.content: This market was the central market for Barcelona until 1973 and its closing marked the beginning of the neighborhood's decline before its current resurgence. While undergoing renovations, whole streets and homes that had been demolished by Phillipe V's orders were discovered and archaeologists who worked to transform the market in to a cultural centre and history museum. Entrance and street level is free, but to visi

voyage.name: Picasso Museum
voyage.price: Adults €13 (on-line €12) , discount for students having student ID & 65+, free on the first Sunday each month, free every Thursday evening from 18:00 to 21:30. Advance booking recommended (including free-of-charge times)
voyage.hours: Sun-Tue 10:00-20:00 (19:00 in winter), closes strictly on time, visitors are asked to exit 10 minutes before closing time. free at certain times, see website.
voyage.content: Has a lot of art from his first period, before the cubism, but almost none of his most famous works. Pictures are described only in Spanish, but overview texts for each period are available in English. Luggage over 30x30cm needs to be left at the checkroom and there's no liability for lost valuables.

voyage.name: Palau Güell
voyage.price: €12 (audio guide included); tickets booth at 1 Nou de la Rambla closes 1 hr earlier; also online
voyage.content: Palace designed by Gaudí for the industrial tycoon Eusebi Güell. There is a basement and three levels of the palace to explore, the highest featuring a small exhibition. It is in a different style to Gaudí's apartment blocks La Pedrera and Casa Batlló, as well as being cheaper and less crowded than those sites. The rooftop of Palau Güell features the more standard Gaudi style chimneys, and views across El Raval.

voyage.name: Plaça Sant Jaume
voyage.content: This square has been the political hub since the Roman era. It has been witness to some of the most important events in modern Catalan history, such as the proclamation of the Catalan State in 1931. At one end, there is the Palace of the Generalitat (the one with two flags on the top, the government of the Autonomous Community of Catalunya) and on the other stands the City Hall (three flags). Both are Gothic building

voyage.name: Plaça Reial
voyage.content: This square is famous for the nightlife and the uniform architecture, and features fountains and palm trees. It was built during the 19th century on the site of a monastery, after the Mendizábal law expelled the monks. After some years Antoni Gaudí designed the streetlights which are still there. It has lots of activity during the day, thanks to the many terraces of the bars and restaurants.

voyage.name: Plaça del Rei
voyage.content: This square has two important buildings, the Santa Àgata church, where the kings from the Aragon crown had baptism. Is possible to visit it. The other building has the Saló del Tinell, one of the best civil Gothic architecture examples. Is the place where the royal receptions where held, so is very wide with a wooden ceiling hold by the typical Catalan Gothic arches. It has also a tower from which you can have a good

voyage.name: Cathedral of Santa Eulàlia
voyage.content: The main Gothic church in Barcelona. The cloister is maybe the most interesting part.

voyage.name: Plaça Sant Felip Neri
voyage.content: One of the most romantic squares in Barcelona, it hides a dark history in that it was built over the city's old cemetery. Barcelona's most famous architect, Antonio Gaudi, was on his way to visit the church there when he was run over and killed in 1928. There is a baroque church (Sant Felip Neri), a 14th-century palace and a fountain in the middle. To arrive, take the narrow street next to the cathedral cloister. The

voyage.name: Plaça del Pi
voyage.content: This square next to La Rambla is one of the prettiest parts of the quarter. It has a pine tree in the middle (Pi mines pine tree), the church of Santa Maria del Pi, which is a very pretty Gothic church with a huge rose window. Many concerts are held here. The Pi square and its twin square, called Sant Josep Oriol, have several bars and artisans, painters, musicians, who are there to sell their products. Entrance into

voyage.name: Carrer Petritxol
voyage.content: This narrow street, that starts in the Plaça del Pi has a very special atmosphere. It is famous because of its chocolate shops, where you can drink a hot chocolate since the 18th century. It has also very important art galleries (Sala Parés, the place where Picasso made a dedicated exposition for the first time). You can enter for free and see, if you are lucky, nice expositions. The street is decorated with flagston

voyage.name: Ancient synagogue
voyage.content: They open during the morning. It is the re-discovered synagogue from the Jewish quarter, called call. This building, not very spectacular, is important since it has been here since the Roman era, and stayed as a synagogue until the Jewish exodus in the 15th century. The guide explains all the facts from the place in several languages.

voyage.name: Museu d'Història de la Ciutat de Barcelona
voyage.content: Includes access to underground Roman ruins and a complex of historic buildings in the centre of the Barri Gòtic (Gothic Quarter), and is a reasonably good historical museum.

voyage.name: Museu de l'Eròtica de Barcelona
voyage.content: Museum dedicated to erotic and sensual works. A huge tourist trap. The tour is not worth it, unless you wish to see old paintings of the Kama Sutra. The only interest is the huge phallus in the hallway, which makes for funny pictures.

voyage.name: Hash Marijuana & Hemp Museum Barcelona
voyage.content: This museum in the modernist Palau Mornau offers a unique permanent exhibition on the development of the cannabis plant as a versatile source for industrial, nutritional, medicinal, sacramental and recreational purposes.

voyage.name: La Rambla
voyage.content: Often the first landmark that people identify with the city. It is the central and most famous boulevard cutting through the heart of the city centre — a vibrant promenade filled with Barcelona life at its best. It stretches from the harbour to La Plaça Catalunya, running through the Ciutat Vella like a spine. Come here to see street performers, enjoy the flower and pet stalls, or just sit back and watch all of Barce

voyage.name: Maritime Museum
voyage.price: 10€ - 18€. Free every Sunday after 3:00 pm. The exhibits in the entrance hall and the Espai Mirador are free of charge
voyage.content: Housed in Drassanes, the Gothic shipyard of the city. During the 14th century, the Aragó Crown was the most important power in the Mediterranean Sea, and this was the main place where the ships were built. Nowadays, it's the Maritime Museum, worth a visit for the architectonic structure, a still-standing part of the ancient medieval city wall (including a gate), and the reproduction of the royal galley of Don

voyage.name: Hospital de la Santa Creu
voyage.content: This Gothic building was the old city hospital, before the modernist Hospital de Sant Pau was built in l'Eixample. Now the hospital has the National Library inside, and is a great example of civilian Gothic archictecture.

voyage.name: Sant Pau del Camp
voyage.content: A rare example of Romanesque architecture, the prettiest in Barcelona. Its name reflects the fact that the church was once surrounded by green fields outside the city walls.

voyage.name: Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona
voyage.content: The arts centre’s core theme is the city and urban culture.

voyage.name: Centre d'Art Santa Mònica
voyage.content: A contemporary art venue, showing solo exhibitions by national and international artists. Lots of other activities.

voyage.name: Barcelona Museum of Contemporary Art
voyage.alt: MACBA, Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 11:00-19:30, Sat 10:00-20:00, Sun 10:00-15:00; Tue Closed except public holidays.
voyage.content: Art from the second half of the twentieth century to today. Smart-phone app with free audio guides.

voyage.name: Museu de les Il·lusions
voyage.content: A museum of more than 30 room-sized, hand-painted 3D murals built on forced perspective: visitors stand on marked spots and appear to hang from a dragon's jaw or teeter over a painted canyon. Photography is the point of the visit.

voyage.name: Aquàrium de Barcelona
voyage.content: The second biggest aquarium in Europe. Watch thousands of fish, penguins and sharks in this interactive sea-life museum. Unlike Genoese Aquarium it has a long glass tube, where you can walk watching sharks and other fish swimming around.

voyage.name: Parc Zoològic de Barcelona
voyage.content: This zoo was famous for its albino gorilla Snowflake prior to his death. Today this zoo still has many other features including a science museum inside the zoo.

voyage.name: Parc de la Ciutadella
voyage.content: Barcelona's most central park, and includes a zoo, a lake and several museums. In fact, the park is so large, 74 acres, that the Catalan Parliament can be found in the centre of the park. It is a great place to enjoy games, sports or to spend a leisurely afternoon. It was built at the final part of the 19th century in the place that formerly occupied the fortress (ciutadella) built after the defeat of 1714. This fort

voyage.name: Port Vell
voyage.content: The harbor was closed to the public until the 80s and received a complete makeover before the Olympics in 1992. Some old buildings related to the harbor still exist, such as the Tinglado near the Barceloneta quarter that is now a history museum. There are two main parts in the harbor: the Moll de la Fusta, which are the decks that touch the city, and the Maremagnum, a newly created amusement centre and shopping mall,

voyage.name: Museum of the History of Catalonia
voyage.price: €6 reductions for 65+, students; children -16 free. Free on the first Su each month
voyage.content: A must in order to understand the troubled and sad history of the Catalans.

voyage.name: Barceloneta Beach
voyage.content: The beach stretches from the tip of Barceloneta in Port Vell and far away, passing Vila Olimpica and further. On warm summer days it will be crammed with people, and it might be a good idea to find a spot further away or go to a beach outside of Barcelona. There is nothing better than covering your toes with sand and lying upwards in the sun, and there is no better place to do this than on Barceloneta's famed beauty.

voyage.name: La Rambla
voyage.content: A gorgeous tree-lined pedestrian walkway, the busiest and most lively street of the city. Mostly occupied by tourists, expect to pay higher prices for food and drink which tends to be low-quality and/or inauthentic. Avoid the groups of people supposedly betting on a game played on a cardboard table, they are thieves. Head off into some of the side streets for a cheaper, more local, and authentic experience of Barcelo

voyage.name: El Portal de l'Àngel
voyage.content: Large pedestrian walkway with many new and stylish shops to browse in.

voyage.name: Sit on Rambla de Mar
voyage.content: Cool your toes at the waters edge: with a book, sandwich or just for a short rest.

voyage.name: Wander the Barri Gotic
voyage.content: 2,000 years of history that remounts to the days when Barcelona was a Roman enclave, uncover charming squares and hidden gems where the locals hang out these days.

voyage.name: Enjoy your Sangria at La Plaça Reial
voyage.content: Great place to sit, relax and drink.

voyage.name: Check out a Flamenco show at Los Torantos
voyage.content: Tarantos is a small bar and theatre. If you just want a half hour taste of Flamenco then check it out. There are 30-minute shows of flamenco song and dance at 20:30, 21:30 and 22:30 nightly. There are plenty of other clubs on the Plaza Reial, but watch out for pickpockets in the early hours of the morning.

voyage.name: Walk around el Born
voyage.content: A very popular area with great restaurants and places to have a few drinks. If your accommodation is on Rambla, Born is a great place to escape the crowds, enjoy a relaxed atmosphere and meet off-the-beaten track travellers and non-tourist-industry locals—especially in the evenings.

voyage.name: Jazz Si
voyage.content: In the Raval neighbourhood. Has a cheaper alternative to flamenco nights elsewhere.

voyage.name: Sip on a coffee in Plaça dels Àngels
voyage.content: During your coffee you can admire the whiteness of the MACBA and the best street skate tricks in town along street art.

voyage.name: Cook&Taste
voyage.content: Cooking class on traditional Spanish dishes. Get ingredients from La Boqueria; then together with a small group led by a professional chef, cook a few dishes: tortilla, paella and crema catalan; and enjoy the meal you prepared.

voyage.name: The Comedy Clubhouse
voyage.content: A stand-up comedy venue in Barcelona. This is the original location, open 3 nights a week with stand-up comedy shows and improv comedy shows. In the past they have enjoyed performances from some of the greats of stand-up comedy including: Louis CK, Trevor Noah, Mark Normand, Michelle Wolf, Kyla Cobbler, Mike Rice.

voyage.name: The Clubhouse Laietana
voyage.content: The new venue of The Comedy Clubhouse, opened in 2025 with a full kitchen with serving North American soul food as well as producing stand-up comedy shows every day of the week and live music, karaoke, pub quizzes etc. Many of the events are completely free, although you are encouraged to eat and drink, whereas the higher end events that they do that feature the best local comedians or international touring comedians

voyage.name: Fnac
voyage.content: Sells books, music, games, and many other interesting items. Fnac is in the El Triangle shopping centre in Plaza Catalunya (Opposite El Corte Inglés).

voyage.name: Maremagnum
voyage.content: Nice shopping mall by the sea at the end of The Ramblas. The only shopping mall in the city open on Sunday and public holidays. Clothes: mostly mass-market brands; no independent designers; only a few outlets of national chains

voyage.name: Barcelona Escuela Mediterráneo
voyage.content: Offers Spanish-language classes. Easy to reach by metro and bus. Near the Ramblas and the beach.

voyage.name: Art Montfalcon
voyage.content: Probably the largest souvenir shop in the city at 1000 m². Almost no ordinary souvenir-shop trivialities; really good choice of creative and artistic souvenirs: watches, plates, jewellery, mugs. Creative mechanical toys: spiders etc. The only missing thing is Kukuxumusu, but there is a choice of other souvenir t-shirt brands.

voyage.name: El Corte Ingles
voyage.content: There are a couple of this nationwide department store chain in the district.

voyage.name: My Beautiful Parking
voyage.content: The bike shop lends bikes too. It is specialised on creating fixies according the customers wishes.

voyage.name: The Most Sustainable Souvenir Shop in the World
voyage.alt: La Tienda de Souvenirs Más Sostenible del Mundo
voyage.content: Operated by Naifactory Lab, this establishment sells souvenirs made locally with the environment in mind.

voyage.name: La Boqueria Market
voyage.content: Tempt your tastebuds at this delightful food market where the food is plentiful, fresh and can be cooked to order in one of about five small restaurants. Also a place for fresh juices and some takeaway snacks. To avoid heavy crowds, or to buy the freshest perishables (e.g., seafood), go well before noon. At least in late Fall, Winter and early Spring months, La Boqueria is closed on Sundays.

voyage.name: Cansaladeria i Formatgeria Josep's
voyage.content: Front-line stand featuring most of hams and meats a tourist needs. Accepts credit cards (!) and has vacuum packaging for any purchase so you don't worry through the rest of the day about smell of all the chorizos you bought.

voyage.name: Happy Pills
voyage.content: A petite candy store located next to the Cathedral Square noted for resembling a pharmacy and packaging their product in plastic medication bottles or first aid kits.

voyage.name: Comite
voyage.content: A group of 7 designers sharing a space where they create and sell their women collections. For women, designers include Cecilia Sorensen, Julia Pelletier, Pia Kahila and Potipoti. For men: Jan iú Més, Bingo and potipoti.

voyage.name: La Gauche Divine
voyage.content: An incredible multiconcept store near La Rambla. An example of the Catalan design is the decoration of the shop with an exclusive combination of furniture from the 1960s and paintings and sculptures all around. The shop includes a little corner where you can have a drink while watching the latest trend publications and an inner patio with plants and sculptures. They have a lot of clothes and accessories for men and w

voyage.name: Amateur
voyage.content: Small boutique shop featuring several independent designers.

voyage.name: Juan-Jo Gallery
voyage.address: C/Elisabets 20, El Raval. 50 meters to MACBA Museum.
voyage.content: Fashion leather. Jackets, bags, hats and complements designed and made in Barcelona with Spanish leather.

voyage.name: Lluch Sabates
voyage.content: Tempting Italian shoe store with gorgeous designs. Features oXs.

voyage.name: Miriam Ponsa
voyage.content: Boutique shop offering designer wares.

voyage.name: Custo Barcelona
voyage.content: Popular designer clothing brand.

voyage.name: Camper
voyage.content: Standalone store having a wide choice of models and sizes.

voyage.name: Atelier Madre - Manuel Dreesmann
voyage.alt: Atelier for Leather Goods and Bags
voyage.content: Atelier for modern minimalistic premium leather goods and bags. All products are traditionally made by hand in the atelier.

voyage.name: Conesa Entrepans
voyage.content: Cheap and very good sandwiches. Always with a lot of people. They have some tables inside. They close quite early at night (by Spanish standards).

voyage.name: Travellers Nest Bar
voyage.content: They serve meals, a full English breakfast and 8oz Irish rump steaks all day with ingredients imported from the UK.

voyage.name: Maoz Vegetarian
voyage.content: Offers excellent vegan falafel (including unlimited salad) for around €4. There are several around Barcelona including one on 95, La Rambla, about 10 minutes walk from Pl Catalunya.

voyage.name: Mercado de La Boqueria
voyage.content: On the Rambla, and offering a wide variety of fresh, mainly raw foods. Some stall sells many kinds of well cooked ready to eat pasta, fresh fruit already sliced. When buying anything here head to the cheaper stalls at the back: you can save a fair bit.

voyage.name: Fres Co
voyage.content: in the shopping centre Maremagnum, store 59. An all-you-can-eat buffet including hot dishes and cold and drink. The bread isn't the greatest, although the vegetable quality is quite good, and the warm food isn't terrible either. Warm food includes whatever soup they have on display, some meats, and pizzas. The Maremagnum buffet has fruit juices, while the one on Plaza Catalunya has numerous desserts, such as an ice c

voyage.name: Bo de B
voyage.address: C/ Fusteria 14 & Carrer de la Mercè
voyage.content: Excellent sandwiches made with freshly chopped/cooked/baked ingredients on fantastic baguette (chicken with avocado sauce is recommended), plates, omelettes and salads for reasonable prices (between €3.50 and 4.50 for a sandwich as of Jan 2016) and generous portions. Service can be a little slow (it's a small place) but it's worth the wait

voyage.name: BioCenter
voyage.content: It offers tasty vegetarian and vegan food.

voyage.name: La Bombeta
voyage.content: Good tapas and more substantial dishes. A great alternative to the tourist traps along the waterfront. Very friendly.

voyage.name: Vegetalia Gòtic
voyage.content: Offers excellent organic vegetarian foods, as a complement to the restaurant there's a store carries the full range of Vegetalia products as well as other well-sourced organic foods. The staff are friendly and the prices reasonable.

voyage.name: Agua
voyage.address: Olympic Port, Passeig Maritim de la Barceloneta, 30
voyage.content: Creative cooking combining Catalonian traditions with Italian cuisine. The terrace outside showcases some great views of Barceloneta.

voyage.name: Bar Bitácora
voyage.content: The bar serves consistently good tapas - patas bravas, platos del dias - for fair price. In the evening many come for a drink.

voyage.name: Cal Pep
voyage.hours: Mon dinner time only; Tue-Sat lunch and dinner time. Closed in Aug
voyage.content: Legendary fish restaurant. With limited seating, the only seats readily available are at the bar if you arrive without a reservation and queue for a while. No menu available, just ask what they have today.

voyage.name: Los Caracoles
voyage.content: Los Caracoles which means "The Snails". You can spot the restaurant right away as it has a spit grill in the main entrance window roasting chickens and other meats. The restaurant was named after its specialty however they offer a wide variety of seafoods and roasted meat dishes.

voyage.name: Bar Pinotxo
voyage.content: The best Catalan dishes. No reservations. Always full, don't be surprised if you aren't able to sit.

voyage.name: Restaurante La Boqueria
voyage.content: An emblematic restaurant in the centre of Barcelona to enjoy the city's local cuisine. Approximately €20 per person to eat dishes like Paella or Tapas.

voyage.name: Restaurante Italiano Rossini
voyage.content: Authentic Italian food in Plaza Real. Homemade pizzas, fresh pasta, Mediterranean tapas, meat and fish. Live piano music every day from 20:00.

voyage.name: My Way Lounge Restaurant
voyage.content: Gourmet Mediterranean cuisine near Plaza Real. Elegant decoration inspired by Art Deco, with paintings by Tamara de Lempicka. It's also a cocktail bar.

voyage.name: The Clubhouse Laietana & Nikki's
voyage.content: The Clubhouse has teamed up with Nikki's and now supply a variety of budget friendly North American soul food. Here you can get fried chicken burgers, fried chicken & waffles, mac & cheese and a whole bunch of other delicious options. They are open for dinner every day of the week.

voyage.name: Can Culleretes
voyage.content: Founded in 1786, it is the second oldest restaurant in Spain (after Casa Botín in Madrid). The prices are mid range and the quality is quite good for the price. They serve traditional Catalan food. But the most interesting from the restaurant is the decoration, an eclectic mix from all the times. A really good option if you don't have much time/money.

voyage.name: La Dolca Herminia
voyage.content: Same chain as Les Quinze Nits. No reservation accepted. Bit old-style and dark interior, judging by web site.

voyage.name: Els Quatre Gats
voyage.content: Frequented by tourists, Els Quatre Gats, is the successor to the famous cafe where Gaudi drank and Picasso exhibited, in a fine Modernisme building by Puig i Cadafalch. The cooking is of a high quality (if it's not onion soup). The wine list (and wine recommendations) can be quite pricey. The decor is quite old fashioned, while the attentive staff are dressed formally. Local visitors for dinner are either over 40s or

voyage.name: Elx Restaurant
voyage.content: Valencian paella and Meditterian dishes. One of the few places available for tourists where paella is genuine enough.

voyage.name: Café Silenus
voyage.content: Also has excellent lunch offers. A design restaurant just in front of the MACBA. Mediterranean and Japanese cuisine.

voyage.name: Al Passatore
voyage.content: Pasta, pizza and risotto in very generous portions for moderate prices. No-frills dishes, but wide choice. Simple interior. Bread should be asked for explicitly. For dinner, reservation essential

voyage.name: Betawi
voyage.content: a really tasty Indonesian restaurant. Portions aren't huge (average) but they know how to cook meat and fish to perfection

voyage.name: Shunka
voyage.content: One of the most appreciated Japanese restaurants in town. Prior reservation is strongly advised.

voyage.name: Cafe de L'Opera
voyage.content: A marvellous place to have a breakfast with fine strong coffee. As the owner insists on coffee and desserts, they are the core competence. The inside features 1920s decor.

voyage.name: Bestial
voyage.content: Fabulous lunch specials to be enjoyed on their great beach terrace on warm sunny days. Dinner tends to be quite expensive, thus lunch is the value for money option.

voyage.name: 7 Portes
voyage.content: This is one of the oldest restaurants in Barcelona. Offers the best Catalan dishes around, at a good price. It's especially famous for its Paella Parellada (rich man's paella, so called because they take the shells off), which is really worth a try. The roast kid (goat) is also a great traditional Catalan dish.

voyage.name: L'Antic Teatre
voyage.content: Screens special artistic productions. There is also a small café inside and outside operated by the association which makes for a great break from the noisy Barcelona downtown. It's only a few steps away from the Palau de la Música Catalana.

voyage.name: Escriba
voyage.content: Very old and beautiful confectionery.

voyage.name: Catwalk
voyage.content: One of the most popular nightclubs in the city, with the peak time around 02:00. They offer 2 floors with R&B and hip-hop styles mixed with House or Techno. A lot of teenagers go here.

voyage.name: Comerç 24
voyage.address: Carrer del Comerç 24, Born, Ciutat Vella
voyage.content: A fashion tapas bar. Very creative, very good.

voyage.name: Danzantoria
voyage.content: House music fans come here for the pumping beats and funky decor. Offers two floors of dancing, and a terrace to chill out on between dances.

voyage.name: La Fianna
voyage.content: One of the busiest bars in the neighborhood with a funky decor and a large selection of spirits. They also have a great dinner menu with an international selection.

voyage.name: Le Kashbar
voyage.content: With a Moroccan decor, Le Kashbar is the perfect spot to chill out on cushions and take in the ambient music.

voyage.name: Opium
voyage.content: Great club. Great music. Dance floor, lounge area, and outside bar.

voyage.name: Cafè Milans
voyage.content: Probably one of the most dynamic bars of the Gothic Area. DJ sessions, live exhibitions, art, and cocktails.

voyage.name: RiBborn
voyage.content: C/Antic de Sant Joan 3. A hip bar in the heart of the Casc Antic, a vibrant section of the Ciutat Vella with a variety of bars and restaurants. RiBborn offers "Funk you till you drop" hiphop jazz reggae and soul with dj Chocolito and guests, Tuesday-Sunday 22:00-03:00. Live music until 01:00 on most Sundays and the odd weeknight.

voyage.name: Shoko
voyage.content: Designed by a Feng Shui expert, Shoko serves you good karma all night. Depending on the night, the dj usually spins House or Hip Hop tunes.

voyage.name: Club Sauvage
voyage.content: One of the best choices for drinks and music in Casc Antic. Offers live music (4 or 5 nights a week, 22:00-00:30). Hosts DJ sessions every night (daily 00:30-04:30/05:00) with DJs of many different styles and from the most important clubs making people dance until the wee hours. Always a good atmosphere.

voyage.name: Travel Bar
voyage.content: Travel Bar is a good place to meet and talk with other people visiting the city. They offer free walking tours guided by long-term 'ex-pat' residents of the city every day at 11:00, 13:00 and 15:00. Has a nice, open terrace. Very much a backpackers' bar, this is a staple hang-out for many travellers. The Travel Bar has a range of activities for every night of the week (pub crawl-like activities are not advertised in

voyage.name: Irish Pub Temple Bar
voyage.content: An Irish pub near Las Ramblas. A space where you can enjoy the best national and international beers, smash burgers, while you watch live games from our big screens.

voyage.name: Irish Pub My Bar
voyage.content: Authentic Irish pub to enjoy the best national and imported beers while you watch live games.

voyage.name: vegan Cat Bar
voyage.content: Well chosen selection of craft beers with good selection of tasty vegan burgers and other dishes. (no fake meat)

voyage.name: Black Lab Brewhouse & Kitchen
voyage.address: Palau del Mar, Pça. de Pau Vila, 1
voyage.content: Closed September 2025. Entry to be removed

voyage.name: Ølgod Brewpub
voyage.content: Craft ale mainly brewed on site.

voyage.name: Gothic Point Hostel
voyage.price: Prices range from €14 in low season to around €20 in high season
voyage.content: Unique dorm design with wooden cubicules allowing more privacy. Free breakfast, 20 minutes daily of free internet access, free Wi-Fi. Free lockers (padlock not included, but on sale in reception for €3).

voyage.name: Hostel Kabul
voyage.content: Has increased its prices considerably to capitalise on its location, popularity and positive guidebook write ups. However it remains friendly and is a magnet for young travellers who come for the party atmosphere. Bookings are available through its web site.

voyage.name: Hostel New York
voyage.content: Youth hostel in Barcelona's Barri Gottic. Includes breakfast, internet, kitchen facilities, and a common room

voyage.name: Residencia Australia
voyage.content: Clean, friendly and good value. Family orientated, they also offer ensuites with kitchenettes and small apartments starting at around €75 per night.

voyage.name: The Welcome INN
voyage.content: An alternative to the typical 'dorm bed' hostel. It offers private rooms (some ensuite doubles, triples, quads) in a large apartment with a modern design and common kitchen and living area.

voyage.name: Pension Alamar
voyage.price: Single rooms from €22; Double rooms from €36; Triple rooms from €55
voyage.content: Pensio Alamar is in the Gothic Quarter, in a pedestrian street near La Rambla. Facilities: kitchen, central heating, air conditioning, telephone, TV room, cradle available for babies up to 2 years, and close parking.

voyage.name: Hostal Quartier Gothic (Barcelona)
voyage.content: The Hostal Quartier Gothic is in the Gothic Quarter near La Rambla

voyage.name: Chic & Basic Tallers
voyage.price: Add 7% VAT to web site prices
voyage.content: Designer-everything self-service pension with entirely white interiors. Personnel can be seen even less often than other travellers. Features: Lacus massage shower, 25" LCD TV and touch-operated lamps in rooms; fridge, bar chairs and Nespresso in the common area. Rooms feature balconies but are not too spacy; WC, shower and a wash-bowl are almost in the room space (and if you close shower you open WC); white floors a

voyage.name: Pension Barcelona City Ramblas
voyage.content: In the central square of Barcelona with La Rambla. Clean rooms with shared bathroom.

voyage.name: Citadines Ramblas Barcelona
voyage.content: All studios and apartments are air-conditioned and have bathrooms equipped with hairdryers, a kitchen, TV with satellite channels, a hi-fi system, a direct-line phone, and safe deposit box.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Central
voyage.content: Close to the Born district, the Grand Hotel Central is in an elegant building dating back to 1926. The stylish bedrooms are generous in space and comfort and emphasise urban modernity through the use of cool, natural materials. Large windows provide rooms with magnificent views and a lot of natural light.

voyage.name: Hotel Barcelona Catedral
voyage.content: A 4-star boutique hotel in the centre. Every Sunday they offer free guided cultural walks through the Gothic quarter.

voyage.name: Hotel California
voyage.content: Renovated gay friendly-budget hotel in the very centre of Barcelona, 100 metres from La Rambla and Placa Reial. Prices start at around €30 per person including breakfast.

voyage.name: Hotel Cuatro Naciones
voyage.content: On La Rambla. Rooms varying from single to quad size.

voyage.name: Hotel Lleó
voyage.content: Two steps from the Rambla, from Plaça Catalunya and from Plaça Universitat.

voyage.name: Hotel Medium Monegal
voyage.content: In the heart of the city, in the Plaza Catalunya, a low budget hotel with 50 rooms, some facing to the Ramblas.

voyage.name: W Barcelona
voyage.address: Plaça de la Rosa dels Vents, 1
voyage.content: Beachfront along Barceloneta boardwalk, the hotel has 473 rooms, including 67 suites, two WOW suites and one Extreme Wow Suite with 360-degree panoramic views.

voyage.name: Pullman Barcelona Skipper
voyage.content: The Skipper is situated at the northwestern tip of Barceloneta's harbour and offers modern design, luxury features and views of either the harbour and sea or inland Barcelona.

voyage.name: Sagrada Família
voyage.alt: Basílica i Temple Expiatori de la Sagrada Família
voyage.price: €26 for adult, with audio guide, €30 if tour included. €10 extra to visit the towers
voyage.content: Barcelona's most popular and famous attraction, the Sagrada Família is a testament to Antonio Gaudi's modernist style and unlike any other church in the world. The texture and detail on the façades are intricate and incorporate forms seen in nature as much of Gaudi's work does. The inside is huge — it's estimated that it can hold 13,000 people — with vaulted ceilings and columns designed to be reminiscent of trees. T

voyage.name: Casa Batlló
voyage.price: Adult €29-€45 (online) discounts for residents, children, students & seniors. demand led pricing.Tickets at counter are €4 more expensive.
voyage.content: Another Gaudi masterpiece along the same avenue as La Pedrera. Open to the public. No straight line or right angles appear anywhere in the house. Often overlooked for La Pedrera, (also by Gaudi), La Casa Batlló is equally as stunning with its unique architecture and infamous two ornamental pillars in the entrance to the terrace. Open for visitors from ground floor to the roof, and down by an old-time elevator.

voyage.name: La Pedrera
voyage.price: from €29, children 0-6 free, discounts for older children, students & 65+. €2 additional charge if buying from ticket office
voyage.content: One of Gaudi's masterpieces, there is not one straight edge on the exterior and the structure is one of Gaudi’s most eccentric and enticing architectural creations. Tours of the interior and the incredible roof structures are available. Great views of the tall buildings (especially La Sagrada Familia) from the roof. Hosts a large exposition of Gaudi works, covering Sagrada Familia and Casa Batlio, not only La Pedrera

voyage.name: Casa Amatller
voyage.price: Audio-guided tour €17 reduced €15: Guided tour €20 reduced €17 (online prices)
voyage.hours: Daily 10:00-19:00 only every 1/2 hr (in English at 11:00); no high heels allowed
voyage.content: Designed by Puig i Cadafalch, the building is a fine work of Modernism. Check the detailed photos and explanation of facade sculptures. It also has a shop that sells fine chocolate (the Amatller family made its money out of cocoa).

voyage.name: Casa Lleó-Morera
voyage.price: Adult €15 (sold online or at Palau de la Virreina (La Rambla, 99)
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-13:30, 15:00-19:00 (only guided tours roughly every 1/2 hr, full tour in English at 11:00)
voyage.content: By Lluís Domènech i Montaner.

voyage.name: Fundació Antoni Tàpies
voyage.content: Created in 1984 by the artist Antoni Tàpies to promote the study and knowledge of modern and contemporary art.

voyage.name: Hotel Majestic
voyage.content: Passeig de Gràcia 68. Enjoy city views from the rooftop. Just enter the elevator right from the lobby, and head up to the top floor.

voyage.name: Plaça de Catalunya
voyage.address: at the end of Passeig de Gràcia and the top of La Rambla
voyage.content: Connecting many of the major streets in the city, the Plaça is a central location and a hub of activity. It is a favourite meeting spot for locals and a transit hub for the tourist buses. There are many fountains, statues and gardens around the plaza, and a number of benches to just sit and take it all in.

voyage.name: Universitat
voyage.content: The university has many interesting buildings, libraries and courtyards.

voyage.name: Street Escape
voyage.content: A scavenger hunt full of puzzles to solve, something like an outdoor escape room, and it doubles as a self-guided tour of modernist architecture around the Casa Batlló. Fun for groups and available in several languages including English. Book in advance.

voyage.name: Bike House Tomas Domingo
voyage.content: The bike shop sells high end bikes.

voyage.name: Cacao Sampaka
voyage.content: Xocoa or The Chocolate Factory is a must for chocolate lovers. They sell special products like peppermint white chocolate or blackberry dark chocolate.

voyage.name: La Concepcio
voyage.content: The local market in the heart of the Eixample sells fresh fruits, vegetables and seafood. This is a great flower market too, the florists are open all week. The market is over than 120 years old, but has been thoroughly modernized since.

voyage.name: Desigual
voyage.content: Different stylish clothes for men, women and children.

voyage.name: Nice Things
voyage.content: There are six shops in Barcelona, this is their outlet.

voyage.name: Nike Store
voyage.content: The Nike shop sells all kinds of football and running shoes. Every Thursday evening they organise a "Run Barcelona" with free participation.

voyage.name: Probike
voyage.content: The bike shop has a wide selection of quality bikes and some interesting offers.

voyage.name: El Corte Ingles
voyage.content: A medium-sized store is to be found at the eastern end of the tram lines in Les Corts, handy if you are after some clothes or other merchandise you may need. Unlike most stores in the chain, in an actually nice and modern building - look for the entrance on the back side of the complex when approaching from Plaça de Francesc Macià (the roundabout)

voyage.name: Restaurant Macrobiòtic Zen
voyage.content: Vegan restaurant.

voyage.name: Vegan Mount
voyage.content: Vegan cafe

voyage.name: La Flauta
voyage.content: Many local business people come to dine here during the week. The ever changing menu del dia (menu of the day) costs around €10 and will fill you up with delicious Catalan cuisine that is well prepared and equally well presented. The Crema Catalana, similar to a creme brulee, makes an excellent choice for dessert. Arriving for lunch before 14:00 could save you from waiting for a table.

voyage.name: El Glop
voyage.content: Catalan meals. Allow about €25 per person, although you could get out of there for half of that if you let the price dictate your choice of dishes.

voyage.name: Le P'ty Mon
voyage.content: The restaurant, formerly known as Ty Bihan, serves good Breton crêpes made with artisanal dough.

voyage.name: El Ùltimo Agave
voyage.content: Authentic Mexican restaurant.

voyage.name: Vinitus
voyage.content: Tapas and seafood

voyage.name: Alba Granados
voyage.content: The restaurant offers pleasant modern Spanish cuisine in a cool setup (wine boxes decorate the walls, the entrance is the local bar). The dessert choices are plenty and the mille-feuille is recommendable.

voyage.name: Cinc Sentits
voyage.content: Named one of the '80 Hottest New Restaurants in the World' by Condé Nast Traveller shortly after opening in 2004, Cinc Sentits surpasses expectations. One of the few restaurants in Barcelona to offer a wine pairing, it features contemporary Catalan cuisine in a modern, warm interior.

voyage.name: Restaurant Gaig
voyage.content: With a reputation for serving the freshest produce around, (there are even chickens wandering around the patio), Gaig focuses on classic Catalan cuisine, but in a modern, lighter sense. The decor is in a contemporary red and black design, and the staff are friendly and welcoming. Was awarded a Michelin Star.

voyage.name: Moo
voyage.content: Renowned Catalan chef Joan Roca serves up tasty treats such as sea bass with lemongrass or a delicious suckling pig.

voyage.name: Bracafe
voyage.content: Nice cosy cafe to sit and lounge over a cup of proper coffee.

voyage.name: Fàbrica Moritz Barcelona
voyage.content: 'Moritz Epidor' absolutely should be tasted. Brewery tours available.

voyage.name: Arena Xperience
voyage.content: 3-story disco club.

voyage.name: BIERCaB
voyage.content: International craft beers a snacks

voyage.name: Maresme Brewery Taproom
voyage.content: Good choice of craft beers. Food available except Monday

voyage.name: Safestay Passeig de Gracia
voyage.content: Formerly Centric Point Hostel.

voyage.name: Hostal Central
voyage.content: Clean, friendly and good value.

voyage.name: St Christopher's Barcelona
voyage.price: From €77 per night which includes a continental breakfast, WiFI and fully laundered beds
voyage.content: Part of the St Christopher's Inns chain, this new hostel has private and dormitory style rooms and a Belushi's bar downstairs.

voyage.name: Hostal Centric Barcelona
voyage.content: Common room, free Wi-Fi, rooms with air-conditioning, heating and TV.

voyage.name: Hostal Que tal Barcelona
voyage.content: In the heart of modernist Barcelona. Gaudi’s Casa Batlló and la Pedrera are a five-minute walk away while las Ramblas, Plaza Cataluña and the Gothic Quarter are all at your doorstep.

voyage.name: Hostal Residencia Australia
voyage.content: Run by a jazz musician, a local politician and an Australian, they have been around for 30 years taking care of guests. Good rooms, all the usual goodies, for couples, creative hearts and all those who want to get a feel of the creative edge of Barcelona in terms of cuisine, art, music, theatre, dance. They love the city and have our own travel guide to show you around. The city is made up of cement buildings, what m

voyage.name: Hostel Barcelona Sant Jordi Alberg
voyage.content: Part of local chain of hostels that operates five hostels in Barcelona. Offers full equipped kitchen, common room with DVD, books, cable TV, guitar and couches, computers with 24 hours free internet access, free lockers and storage room, laundry facilities, towels rentals and public phone.

voyage.name: Jardinets Guest House
voyage.price: From €50 double room, breakfast and WiFi included
voyage.content: The beautiful building breaths the atmosphere of the late 19th century, which also is reflected in the inside. You'll find it relaxed and well preserved. Free access to the fridge, microwave and all the ingredients to prepare yourself a varied Mediterranean-style breakfast.

voyage.name: Pere Tarrés Youth Hostel
voyage.content: A hostel near the top of Diagonal. It is very safe and good fun, offering a restaurant, bar, TV area, ping-pong tables, kitchen, free internet, and sheets and breakfast included in the price. Be sure to book online; there are often good deals on the hostel's website.

voyage.name: Urbany Hostel Barcelona
voyage.content: It's located in the Sant Marti district, but close to the eastern border of the Eixample. Twins, 4-, 6-, 8-person dorms - en-suite bathrooms, fitness club and swimming pool, breakfast included, security lockers, wifi throughout the building, common room with cheap bar.

voyage.name: Hotel Soho Barcelona
voyage.content: A design hotel built in 2006. Offers 54 modern and spacious rooms and a rooftop deck with pool. Free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: B-Hotel
voyage.content: A modern urban hotel by prestigious architect Alfredo Arribas. On the 8th floor you can find the endless-pool with views over Plaza Espanya and Montjuic hill. Free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Hotel Granvia
voyage.content: Built in 1870 as a palace for the Serra-Chopitea family, the building was converted into a hotel in 1935. Today it still stores countless pieces and works of art from the 19th century, making it at once a distinguished, elegant and unique hotel. Free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Hotel Villa Emilia
voyage.content: A modern boutique hotel, built in 2006. The hotel is also home to the popular Zinc bar.

voyage.name: 987 Barcelona Hotel
voyage.content: New modern design hotel, free WiFi.

voyage.name: Hotel del Comte
voyage.content: 1 km from La Rambla. Super-slick rooms with glass and marble bathrooms, flat panel TVs, free Wi-Fi. Problems with 3rd-party bookings reported, so book directly.

voyage.name: Best Western Premier Hotel Regina
voyage.content: About €100 per night for a double room with bath and breakfast.

voyage.name: Expo Hotel Barcelona
voyage.content: 425 wifi-equipped rooms, near Sants Central Station and Fira (Expo). €58-180.

voyage.name: Granados 83
voyage.content: Enric Granados 83. Set in a 19th-century hospital, it has been converted into a Nouveau Art Decó styled hotel. Its structure of oxidised iron is reminiscent of New York's Soho loft, and it stands in contrast with the stone and glass façade and the elegant, minimalist zen styled interiors.

voyage.name: Hotel Gran Via
voyage.address: Gran Via de les Corts Catalanes, 642
voyage.content: Very central. As a former palace, the public spaces of the hotel live up to its history. The rooms are large, but otherwise relatively modest. About €80 per night for a double room with bath.

voyage.name: Hotel Best Aranea
voyage.content: Nice hotel near the Sagrada Familia cathedral.

voyage.name: ibis Styles Barcelona Centre
voyage.content: Economical hotel with inclusive breakfast

voyage.name: Hotel Omm
voyage.content: In Passeig de Gràcia district, featuring elegant rooms with adaptable lighting.

voyage.name: Hotel Majestic
voyage.content: Established in 1918. Its rooftop terrace "La Dolce Vitae" offers views of La Sagrada Familia and much of the city.

voyage.name: Renaissance Barcelona
voyage.content: In a rather nondescript building, the Renaissance offers contemporary style typical for the chain - except for guest bathrooms, who seem to have evaded renovation.

voyage.name: Alexandra Barcelona A DoubleTree by Hilton
voyage.content: The Alexandra's rooms are somewhat sombre, with minimal decor kept in grayish hues. The lobby and restaurant are very impressive, however.

voyage.name: Hotel Indigo Barcelona - Plaza Catalunya
voyage.address: Gran Via de les Corts Catalanes 629
voyage.content: Trying to make the most out of a very small building in the Gran Via.

voyage.name: NH Podium
voyage.content: The usual NH fare packed into a nice corner building a minute away from the Arc de Triomf.

voyage.name: El Palace Hotel
voyage.address: Gran Via de les Corts Catalanes 668 Eixample

voyage.name: Park Güell
voyage.price: €10; reduced €7.00, children until 6 - free ticket required
voyage.hours: Oct 25-Mar: 08:30-18:15; Mar Sep7-Oct24: 08:00-20:00; May-Sep 6: 08:00-21:30; (last entry 30-45 min earlier)
voyage.content: A large urban park heavily influenced by Antonio Gaudi. The area was originally meant to be a residential property development with Gaudi doing much of the planning and landscape design. Only two houses were built and the land was later sold to the city of Barcelona and turned into a park. There are two areas -- a relatively undeveloped (and un-crowded) natural area near the top of the hill and the more famous sculpt

voyage.name: Park Güell, the main entrance
voyage.content: Two Gaudi-style pavilions mark the entrance to the park and lead to the steps up to the Hipostila Room. In the middle of the steps is the dragon (or salamander) fountain that has become almost as much a symbol of Barcelona as the Sagrada Familia.

voyage.name: Hipostila Room and Grand Plaza
voyage.content: At the top of the stairs from the main entrance is the Hipostila Room with its 86 white columns supporting the plaza above. The ceiling has a number of colourful mosaics. Above the Hipostila Room is the main terrace, which was meant to be the main square of the development. It features a mosaic-tiled wall in the shape of an undulating sea serpent and provides excellent views of Barcelona.

voyage.name: Gaudi House Museum
voyage.hours: From 1 January 2024, the Gaudí House Museum will be closed for maintenance and renovations.
voyage.content: Distinctive pink house that Gaudi lived in for nearly 20 years (although not designed by him). It features furniture designed by Gaudi and other objects relating to Gaudi's life. The gift shop has a large selection of Gaudi-themed souvenirs that are generally better quality than what's available in the normal tourist shops.

voyage.name: Turo de les tres creus
voyage.content: This is the highest point of the park and where Gaudi wanted to build a chapel. After the development failed, Gaudi built a monolith with three crosses like Calvary instead. Be sure to take in the panoramic views of Barcelona.

voyage.name: Casa Vicens
voyage.hours: Mon 10:00-15:00, last admission 13:40, Tue-Sun 10:00-19:00, last admission 17:40
voyage.content: The first building Gaudi built in Barcelona. It has been opened as a museum. It's possible to walk the whole monumental enclosure, including the garden and the interior of the building. In UNESCO World Heritage Sites list since 2005.

voyage.name: Bosque Multicines
voyage.content: The cinema has 9 screens.

voyage.name: Cines Verdi
voyage.content: The cinema screens a diverse programme of independent, mainly European and Asian films. All films are shown in their original version.

voyage.name: Teatre Lliure
voyage.content: This alternative theatre offers high quality plays.

voyage.name: Centre Artesà Tradicionarius
voyage.content: Folk & world music

voyage.name: Boo
voyage.content: Besides clothing and accessories for men and women from interesting brands, the shop sells books and perfumes.

voyage.name: GreenLifeStyle
voyage.content: The shops philosophy is based on principles of sustainability, recycling and fair trade, which all sold items adhere. One finds cute designer dresses for a fair price.

voyage.name: Pinc Store
voyage.content: Anna Tichy sells her design clothes, including dresses and swim wear.

voyage.name: graciadorada
voyage.content: The shop sells women fashion including dresses, skirts and jewelery.

voyage.name: Mercat de l’Abaceria
voyage.content: Built in 1892 the market sells local vegetables, fruits, fish, meat, cheeses and herbs. The market has three bars, all of which sell food prepared with ingredients from the market.

voyage.name: Mercat de la Libertat
voyage.content: The market opened in 1888 and designed by architect Miquel Pasqual i Tintoré, it was modernised by a complete renovation. It sells poultry, game and eggs, Spanish hams and sausages, meat and offal, fruit and vegetables, pulses and cereals, farm produce, fresh fish and seafood, salted fish, preserves and provisions and bakery.

voyage.name: Mercat de Lesseps
voyage.content: Inaugurated in 1974 it is an indoor market.

voyage.name: Planeta Te
voyage.content: The shop sells a big variety of different teas: green, black, oolong and infusions.

voyage.name: Verema i collita
voyage.content: Sympatic cellar with good choices for local wines and cava.

voyage.name: Hibernian
voyage.content: Good selection in many categories. Also has some new books, and a shelf of German and French titles.

voyage.name: Intersport
voyage.content: The shop sells all kind of back-packs and outdoor equipment including skis, snow-boards and climbing gear.

voyage.name: Nus
voyage.content: Since more than 30 years this shop sells outdoor gear specialised for activity in the mountains including speleology. The owner knows the surroundings of Barcelona and can give you great tips for Pyrenees trips.

voyage.name: Frankfurt's Casa Valles
voyage.content: Sells hamburgers and hot dogs at cheap prices, hence very popular for locals and young crowd in the evenings.

voyage.name: La Caravana
voyage.content: A Syrian restaurant

voyage.name: Bar Chato
voyage.address: Carrer de Calderón de la Barca, 111

voyage.name: Restaurant La Salut
voyage.address: Carrer de la Mare de Déu de la Salut, 16

voyage.name: Veg World - India
voyage.content: A restaurant that serves only vegetarian food - mainly Indian dishes. This may be the only place in Barcelona where you can get Masala Dosa. Beware that the size of the dishes is not that big.

voyage.name: Can Xurrades
voyage.content: Probably one of the best Catalan restaurants in the neighbourhood, although their selection of other Spanish food is quite good. Particularly excels at meat dishes, cooked in traditional Catalan style. Dishes of note include the Ous Estrellats (Andalusian scrambled eggs with potato) as well as desserts such as strawberries with salt and pepper. Great wine selection with a number of Catalan varieties.

voyage.name: Karakala
voyage.content: The Lebanese restaurant has impeccable and friendly service. It serves authentic Lebanese food.

voyage.name: Kibuka
voyage.content: The Japanese sushi bar serves in convivial atmosphere different sushi plates, Japanese beer, sake, cocktails and wines too.

voyage.name: La Rosa del Desierto
voyage.content: The Moroccan food restaurant in Barcelona offering quality and generous portions, with a quite special decoration.

voyage.name: Sol i Lluna
voyage.content: This cosy restaurant serves good Mediterranean cuisine.

voyage.name: La Taberna del Cura
voyage.price: 1st courses €4-12; main courses €12-20; salad, filet, small bottle wine, water, dessert, coffee - €50
voyage.content: Known by locals as one of the better restaurants in town, the menu is mostly meat selections, but seafood can be ordered from its sister restaurant Botafumeiro next door. La Taberna is on the expensive side, but the food is excellent.

voyage.name: Taverna El Glop
voyage.content: Catalan meals. Allow about €20 per person, although you could get out of there for half of that if you let the price dictate your choice of dishes. See chain review in the Eat section of Barcelona.

voyage.name: Alkimia
voyage.price: €130 taster menu, €68 traditions dinner menu, €39 midday menu
voyage.content: One of Barcelona's most highly regarded restaurants, run by acclaimed restaurateur Jordi Vilà. With a minimalist white interior that directs the attention to the inventive and indulgent foods on offer, Alkimia spearheads a new wave of new Catalan cooking that will delight and impress. It was awarded a Michelin Star.

voyage.name: Botafumeiro
voyage.content: Next door to La Taberna Del Cura, Botafumeiro specializes in seafood, while La Taberna handles the meats. High quality food with a price tag to match.

voyage.name: D.O. vins i platillos
voyage.content: The wine bar offers exquisite tapas and many local wine choices.

voyage.name: Somodo
voyage.price: lunch menu €18.50, tasting dinner menu €25 (excluding taxes)
voyage.content: The small hidden gem has 19 tables, hence reservation is highly recommended. The chef Hojiro Ochi serves Mediterranean cuisine with Japanese influences. The tasting menu consists of 3 entrées, 2 main dishes (fish and meat) and 3 desserts. If you are vegetarian it is recommended to declare it in advance when booking the table. The ingredients are chosen carefully at the Boqueria market. The elaborate kitchen links tra

voyage.name: Bobby Gin S.L.
voyage.content: This stylish cocktail bar offers many different Gin Tonic's. Expect to wait a little at the door.

voyage.name: El Dorado
voyage.content: With an ample dance floor, it also has a pool table, 'futbolín' and arcade games. The giant video screens and the monitors over the bar are other icons of this music bar. Drinks are catered for by staff that are professional, likeable and friendly.

voyage.name: La Cervesera Artesana
voyage.content: Barcelona's first brew-pub still going strong. Tasty snacks to go with the beer.

voyage.name: Café del Sol
voyage.content: An emblem, Cafè del Sol was one of the first bars to open in this famous and very popular Gràcia squares. There is a decent choice of tapas or sandwiches too. Inside has a marble bar, outside many chairs on the placa.

voyage.name: Bodevici
voyage.content: The organic ice cream shop uses organic milk and fruits for natural flavours. They have sorbets like mango or red fruits and chocolate ice creams.

voyage.name: Ottimo Gelats
voyage.content: The ice cream is hand made. The service is great and allows you different mixes. One of the best ice creams in town.

voyage.name: Pensión Norma
voyage.content: Modest rooms, some with bath, about a kilometre north of the centre of town.

voyage.name: Sant Jordi Hostel Gracia
voyage.content: The hostel has mixed dorms for 4 to 8 people. It is open 24 hours a day. Fully equipped kitchen.

voyage.name: Hotel Casa Fuster
voyage.content: Hotel Casa Fuster's Barcelona accommodation offers 105 rooms. The stunningly beautiful, iconic 19th-century building is at the head of the chic Passeig de Gracia Avenue. It has a roof terrace with a pool and excellent views.

voyage.name: El Palauet
voyage.content: El Palauet Living Barcelona boutique hotel, with 8 suites and a spa is found on the most exclusive boulevard, in a five-storey palatial mansion built in 1906, that is an extraordinary example of Modernisme (the sumptuous Catalan version of Art Nouveau).

voyage.name: Torre Glòries
voyage.content: Formerly known as Torre Agbar. Distinctively-shaped office tower which stands out in the Barcelona skyline. It stands out even more Friday, Saturday and Sunday nights when it is lighted in several colours. The viewing platform on the 30th floor has views in all directions. Tickets start at €15 and come with a complimentary glass of cava and access to Hyperview Barcelona, an exhibit of the city’s real-time environment

voyage.name: DHub Disseny Hub Barcelona
voyage.price: General admission/reduced admission: permanent exhibitions €6 reduced €4; temporary exhibitions €4.40/3; combined permanent and temporary exhibitions €8/5.50. Tickets valid for any 2 days within the 6 months following purchase.
voyage.content: Much to the dismay of Mickey Mouse aficionados, Disseny is Catalan for "design", not "Disney". The "Disseny Hub" houses the amalgamated museums focusing on applied arts and design, including Museu de les Arts Decoratives, Museu de Ceràmica, Museu Tèxtil i d'Indumentària and Gabinet de les Arts Gràfiques. The new building has an intricate, multi-level structure, with the protruding tower overhanging the Praca de les G

voyage.name: Museu de Ciències Naturals de Barcelona
voyage.hours: Oct-May: Tue-Fri 10:00-19:00; Sat Sun 10:00-20;00; June-Sept: Tue-Sun 10:00-21:00
voyage.content: Museum with a number of exhibitions about the Earth and its natural history. One exhibit covers the origin of life on Earth and how it has evolved. A second exhibit deals with nature and life on Earth today. The third exhibit covers some of the issues relating to humans and their relationship with nature.

voyage.name: Olympic Port
voyage.content: It has a large number of restaurants, bars and other establishments. In this wide offer you can find also the Barcelona Casino.

voyage.name: Torre d'aigües de Macosa
voyage.content: One of the most unusual landmarks in this otherwise ultra-modern area is this 19th-century (finished in 1882) brick water tower. Standing 62 metres tall, it is now overshadowed by neighbouring residential, office and hotel towers and easy to miss unless you know where to look for it.

voyage.name: Parc Diagonal Mar
voyage.content: Urban park created from redeveloping industrial land. It covers 14 hectares and includes seven areas like a children's play area, a lake with sculptures and a central plaza.

voyage.name: Nova Icària
voyage.content: Next to the Port Olympic, has easy access to restaurants and shopping.

voyage.name: Mar Bella
voyage.content: Mar Bella is considered the nudist beach for Barcelona

voyage.name: Les Glòries
voyage.content: A large shopping centre by the Diagonal, right at the Plaza Glories. Includes a large Carrefour supermarket, a cinema and a number of the usual chain stores, including Zara, H&M and C&A. There is also in. al. a drugstore, optician and a post office.

voyage.name: Centro Commercial Diagonal Mar
voyage.content: Another shopping centre at the opposite end of the Diagonal. A similar selection of tenants, including a cinema.

voyage.name: Vegan Food Heaven
voyage.content: Bright & airy vegan fusion restaurant. on-line table reservation.

voyage.name: L’Ovella Negra (The Black Sheep)
voyage.content: A great place to meet up with a large group of friends or to make a large group of new friends! It is a beer hall styled in a traditional Catalan manner. It has been around for decades in the Poble Nou district of Barcelona. It has huge wooden tables that seat no less than ten people. It has exposed stone walls and large wood supports so you feel you are in a barn or old farm house. The Black Sheep is also immediatel

voyage.name: Razzmatazz
voyage.content: Large and popular club with several rooms, each one a different style of music (pop, retro, house, trance). It is loved by the visitors and locals. €15 will get you in with a free drink. It's worth paying an entry fee. Saturdays at 02:00 is the absolute best time to go, and worth the 5-minute and 400-m line to get in. Closes at 06:00. Note: If you are going to see something at Razzmatazz 2 or 3, the entrance is throu

voyage.name: Travelodge Barcelona Poblenou
voyage.content: Given the popularity of Spain among British vacationers it is no wonder that Britain's favourite budget lodging chain finally got a pied-a-terre in Barcelona. Just like any other Travelodge, it is as simple as can be, but just as cheap.

voyage.name: Hotel BestPrice Diagonal
voyage.content: This simple new hotel tries to live up to its name by undercutting competition by a wide margin.

voyage.name: Catalonia Albeniz
voyage.content: A simple and slightly dated hotel right next to the Clot train station.

voyage.name: Catalonia Atenas
voyage.content: One of the three Catalonia hotels in the area, this one is a tad north from the Clot train station. Rooms are small, fixtures and furniture have their best times behind them but prices are very reasonable.

voyage.name: Catalonia Sagrada Familia
voyage.content: A sister property to the Catalonia Albeniz, it is a simple and slightly aged hotel squeezed into a block a very short distance from the Clot train station. The Sagrada Familia itself is six blocks away towards the southwest.

voyage.name: Four Points by Sheraton Barcelona Diagonal
voyage.content: The Four Points offers simply furnished yet sunny rooms thanks to floor-to-ceiling windows, straight on the Diagonal.

voyage.name: Hotel Front Maritim
voyage.content: The hotel is very aptly named, as it faces the sea directly across the Nova Mar Bella beach. As the property has aged quite badly by the beginning of the 21st century, it offers relatively attractive prices.

voyage.name: Hesperia del Mar
voyage.content: Old-style Spanish vacation hotel (CRT TVs in rooms!) is close to the Mar Bella beach. Do note that the hotel is sideways versus the sea, so not all rooms have the same brilliant views.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Express Barcelona City 22@
voyage.content: A little run down Holiday Inn Express offers some of the cheapest hotel stays in Barcelona with breakfast included.

voyage.name: ibis Barcelona Plaza Glories 22@
voyage.content: This is a standard ibis hotel, despite its name not really close to the Plaza Glories. Of note is the fact that no twin rooms are offered, only doubles.

voyage.name: NH Diagonal Center
voyage.content: The hotel is not really on or near the Diagonal, nor especially central, but all in all offers the usual NH standard in the middle of Sant Marti.

voyage.name: Tryp Barcelona Condal Mar
voyage.content: In a round modern tower a few blocks north of the Diagonal. Typical Tryp features, including family rooms with foldaway bunk beds.

voyage.name: Vincci Bit
voyage.content: This unexpectedly stylish hotel is two blocks towards the north from the Diagonal shopping centre. Each floor's corridor is decorated in a different, unusual theme and the cheerful yet tasteful variety of decor makes up for quite small and simple rooms. For thrifty holidaymakers, a Lidl supermarket is around the corner

voyage.name: Vincci Maritimo
voyage.content: The other Vincci is just as maritime as any other hotel in Sant Marti, as it is actually close to the Diagonal and not the seaside. It is also less adventurous in style, but nonetheless very pleasantly and contemporarily outfitted.

voyage.name: AC Hotel Barcelona Forum by Marriott
voyage.content: The AC is basically a part of the Convention Centre, towering over its meeting spaces. It features an unusually contemporary design theme for a Marriott-branded property.

voyage.name: Barcelo Atenea Mar
voyage.content: Right at the Nova Mar Bella beach

voyage.name: Barcelona Princess
voyage.content: The Princess occupies a tower at the very tip of the Diagonal, boasting great views in all directions and a very metropolitan ambience. The postmodern design mix is enhanced in some rooms appointed with lavishly colourful decorations and patterns by the Spanish apparel brand Desigual.

voyage.name: Confortel Barcelona
voyage.content: There is nothing really special about the Confortel, apart from really small windows. Rooms are quite sombre and the building is squeezed into one of the blocks at Poblenou.

voyage.name: H10 Marina Barcelona
voyage.content: A long shot (five blocks) from the actual marina in the Olympic Port, the H10 is a regular midmarket city hotel with a selection of 235 rooms in different sizes and standards. A rooftop terrace with a pool provides a nice overview of Poblenou.

voyage.name: Hilton Diagonal Mar Barcelona
voyage.content: Adjacent to the Congress Centre and facing the Centro Commercial Diagonal Mar.

voyage.name: Melia Barcelona Sky
voyage.content: Upscale hotel in Poble Nou neighbourhood. Amenities include free high-speed internet, minibars in all rooms, 24 hour access to the gym, pillow-top mattresses and a pillow menu.

voyage.name: Novotel Barcelona City
voyage.content: The Novotel boasts a brilliant location on the Diagonal, with excellent views of the neighbouring Agbar Tower, especially from its rooftop pool and terrace. Regular rooms are of the usual old Novotel standard, the upscale categories have been renovated and feature a more modern, edgy design with the use of dark colours.

voyage.name: Hotel SB Diagonal Zero
voyage.price: Rooms start from €120 and suites start from €290 (summer)
voyage.content: 262 rooms and suites, with many having sea views. Amenities include free Wifi, a fitness room, spa, executive floor and a pool with views from the 17th floor.

voyage.name: Hotel SB Icaria Barcelona
voyage.price: Rooms start from €150 and suites start from €185 (summer)
voyage.content: Modern hotel close to the beach and Port Olimpic. Amenities include free Wifi, a solarium with a pool and fitness room. Some rooms are suites with either a study (for business) or a jacuzzi.

voyage.name: Silken Diagonal Barcelona
voyage.content: Postmodern extravaganza right next door to the Agbar tower.

voyage.name: Hotel & Spa Villa Olimpic
voyage.content: This hotel with a spa is actually a bit north of the actual Olympic Village. Due to its constrained location within one of the old blocks of Poblenou, the experience there may be less rewarding than in some of the newer hotels.

voyage.name: Hospital de la Santa Creu i Sant Pau
voyage.price: Adult €18, guided visit €21 (see web site for schedules and other options)
voyage.content: This former hospital is an architectural masterpiece that is now open for visitors. Inpatient wards (and most outpatient facilities) have been moved to a new building of Nou Hospital, but in terms of touring the area, that makes it all the easier. One of "small hidden features" is a network of underground passages where small carriages can be seen, you can get there near WCs on a central square, between Banc de Sang

voyage.name: Monestir de Pedralbes
voyage.price: €5; reduced €3.50. 1st Su of the month and Su after 15:00 free
voyage.content: A beautiful Gothic monastery near the university, there are a museum which depicts the monastery life, a church, and a marvelous chapel covered with medieval frescoes.

voyage.name: Pavellons de la Finca Güell
voyage.content: A complex of two pavilions by Antonio Gaudi. 2024 closed for renovation.

voyage.name: MMACA - Museu de Matemàtiques de Catalunya
voyage.hours: Wed 17:00-20:00; Sun 10:00-14:00. Sometimes open on additional days but closed during school holidays.
voyage.address: Can Mercader Palace, Hospitalet Road, s/n 08940 Cornellà de Llobregat
voyage.content: The museum has limited opening hours but the park it is situated in is also interesting. Check website before going to the museum as it will eventually relocate to The Can Bagaria building.

voyage.name: Camp Nou
voyage.content: If you're a football fanatic, then you can't miss a visit to this football temple, the home ground for Barcelona's biggest and most popular team and one of Europe's greatest footballing 'cathedrals'. During the Franco era, FCB was the only way that oppressed Catalans could vent their anger against his dictatorship. Because of that, it became and still is a symbol of Catalan identity. Camp Nou is the biggest stadium i

voyage.name: Futbol Club Barcelona Museum
voyage.price: €25 (€20 for people from 6-13 and >70 years old)
voyage.hours: 09:00-19:00; Dec 25, Jan 1 closed (deviating on match days)
voyage.content: Museum dedicated to the FC Barcelona. It occupies 3,500 m² and attracts 1.2 million visitors a year, ranking it second to the Museu Picasso, which attracts 1.3 million visitors, as the most visited museum in the city of Barcelona. All of the Barcas trophies and jerseys of many famous players of the team are exhibited. The museum can be visited by booking the Camp Nou Experience package, which includes also a stadium

voyage.name: CosmoCaixa
voyage.price: €8 for general admission. Some exhibitions & activities have an additional charge.
voyage.content: Isaac Newton 26; Perhaps one of the best science museums in Europe. Order tickets online to avoid the queue. Depending on your level of interest, you can spend there up to half a day. Plenty of fun interactive elements. Weekends may be crowded.

voyage.name: Tibidabo
voyage.content: Located on the mountains of Barcelona (farther north from Gracia) and offers a spectacular view of the city (532 m high). This is a place where according to some legends, the Devil tempted Jesus Christ offering him the whole world in exchange for his worship. At the top there is an awesome church, which offers panoramic views of the city. The church is almost completely surrounded by a big amusement park. You will al

voyage.name: Tramvia Blau
voyage.content: It is an old tram (beginning of the 20th century) connecting Av. Tibidabo metro station and Funicular station at the foot of Tibidabo. As of November 2017, closed for maintenance. Use bus 196 instead, which is also cheaper and covered by metro tickets. Bus station are located 50 meters up the hill from the Tramvia Blau station.

voyage.name: Funicular del Tibidabo
voyage.price: €12; free if bought with the €35 amusement park admission
voyage.content: It connects the terminus of Tramvia Blau at the Plaça del Doctor Andreu with an amusement park at the summit of the Tibidabo mountain. It's an underwhelming ride. Trees block the view throughout the ride.

voyage.name: Funicular de Vallvidrera
voyage.price: As per Integrated Fare System tariff. (Zone 1)
voyage.content: A much cheaper (and still fast) way is to take suburban train to Peu del Funicular, then ride up to Vallvidrera Superior by the Vallvidrera Funicular (a free connection in Peu del Funicular train station). From there, take bus No 111 (also a free connection) to the top of the mountain.

voyage.name: Parc del Laberint d'Horta
voyage.content: Try out the labyrinth in the centre of this park. The park also has a nice waterfall, a romantic canal and gardens. A quiet place to relax for several hours away from the busy city. Wheelchair accessible. Free of charge on Wednesdays and Sundays.

voyage.name: Ronda Verde
voyage.content: Bike, run or walk along part of the Ronda Verde, which runs around the edge of the hills to the north of the city and offers great views.

voyage.name: Custo Barcelona
voyage.content: Popular designer clothing brand.

voyage.name: L'illa
voyage.content: A nice modern shopping mall located on Avinguda Diagonal, Barcelona's main transport artery. Contains many mid-range to high end brands.

voyage.name: La Riera
voyage.content: Vegetarian restaurant with varied menu that uses seasonal ingredients from local markets.

voyage.name: Can Punyetes
voyage.content: A very traditional Catalan restaurant favored by locals. Menu in Catalan, but it's worth the risk, the food is delicious.

voyage.name: Flash-Flash
